decisions.quote: We replicated our previous work with 11 of the same participant pairs—6 individuals with hippocampal amnesia and 5 comparison participants—each of whom was paired with a familiar partner of their choosing. Focusing on the productions of the partners (i.e., partners became directors) we (1) coded referential expressions as definite or indefinite; (2) tracked changes in the use of indefinite and definite references across trials; and (3) compared data to previous analyses (when amnesia participants were directors).
decisions.reason: Both shipped and blind coding agree the study is a replication. The authors collected new barrier-task data at least 6 months later with communication partners switching roles to serve as directors, re-testing and directly comparing against their prior finding on definite reference use in hippocampal amnesia.

corrected_value.title: The use of definite references signals declarative memory: Evidence from hippocampal amnesia
corrected_value.authors: Duff MC, Gupta R, Hengst J, Tranel D, Cohen NJ

decisions.quote: Of particular interest was how similar the use of definite initiating reference in the present study, when the familiar partners of the amnesia participants were the directors, when compared with our previous work ( Duff et al., in press ), when the amnesia participants were the directors. When the amnesia participants were the directors, 56% (967) of the initiating references were coded as definite compared to 48% (825) of initiating references coded as definite in the current study when the familiar partners were the directors.
decisions.reason: Wrong original in shipped row: Duff et al. (2006) (10.1038/nn1601) only supplied the barrier task protocol, whereas Duff et al. (in press) (10.1177/0956797611404897) is the paper that reported the definite-referencing finding when amnesia participants were directors and is the target finding re-tested and compared against here. Blind target 0 matches shipped row 195.

decisions.quote: The data displayed that the difference between amnesia and comparison pairs in the use of indefinite references observed in Duff et al. (in press) was not limited to the productions of the amnesia participants but also extended to their partners without brain damage. Specifically, the healthy familiar partners of the amnesia participants used a definite reference to initiate referencing with their profoundly memory impaired partner less than half as often as the directors of the comparison pairs without brain damage.
decisions.reason: The replication confirmed the original finding from Duff et al. (in press): just as when amnesia participants were directors (56% vs. 90% definite references), pairs managing amnesia used significantly fewer definite initiating references than comparison pairs when their healthy partners were directors (48% vs. 95%, p = .01) and transitioned more gradually to assured definite forms. The shipped quote ('In sharp contrast...') contrasts the amnesia group with the healthy comparison group rather than contrasting the replication with the original study.

decisions.quote: The current study replicated the barrier protocol from our previous work with pairs managing amnesia ( Duff, Hengst, Tranel, & Cohen, 2006 ) and focuses on the productions of their communication partners.
decisions.reason: Blind target 0 (Duff et al., in press, 10.1177/0956797611404897) is not an omitted second target; it is the single target of this replication and pairs with shipped row 195 (which mistakenly cited the 2006 protocol paper 10.1038/nn1601 as the original).
